subtasks.goal: Revenue Ops has reported that the same CRM problem has been logged multiple times as separate tickets and nobody is picking it up. Using the support desk tools: 1) List all open (and new) CRM tickets and read the full detail of each one to understand the actual problem described, impact scope, links, and comments. 2) Identify which of these tickets genuinely describe the same underlying incident (not just superficially similar CRM issues) — read each ticket carefully before deciding, since only true duplicates should be merged; leave any ticket that is a distinct problem untouched. 3) For the set of genuine duplicates, merge them into a single survivor ticket: the survivor must be the earliest-created report among the duplicates, and it must carry the earliest SLA deadline of the whole set (check each ticket's existing SLA deadline before choosing — if none of them has a deadline yet, you will need to determine the correct one per the severity/response-target rules below and set it before or as part of the merge). Every reference to a merged ticket must move to the survivor. 4) Determine the correct severity for the surviving ticket: call get_escalation_matrix for the crm service and read off the severity that corresponds to the survivor's (post-merge, broadest) impact scope — do not guess it. Set that severity on the survivor ticket with set_severity. 5) If the survivor ticket has no SLA deadline yet, set one using extend_sla to the current time (get_current_time) plus the response target for that severity from the escalation matrix; never move an already-committed deadline earlier, only later or leave it if it's already earliest per the merge rule above. 6) Determine the correct rotation that owns the crm service from the escalation matrix, then call get_oncall for that rotation with an explicit `at` parameter equal to the survivor ticket's SLA deadline (not the current time) to find the correct engineer. Assign the survivor ticket to that engineer using assign_ticket. 7) Post a comment on the survivor ticket summarizing which tickets were merged into it, why they were judged to be the same incident, and the resulting severity/assignment. Do not touch, merge, or re-grade any CRM ticket that is not part of this genuine duplicate set.
